summary:
FIELD SHIFT is a smart agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make better crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data and climate analysis.

Our project addresses the challenges of climate change, water scarcity, unpredictable rainfall, and soil degradation by transforming complex environmental data into practical agricultural insights.

We developed a user-friendly platform that allows farmers to select their farm location, explore local climate conditions, and receive crop rotation recommendations. The project uses NASA POWER climate data and incorporates analysis of MODIS vegetation and land surface temperature observations. Python-based data processing and agricultural knowledge support the evaluation of environmental conditions and potential crop suitability.

FIELD SHIFT aims to help farmers understand their land, explore more sustainable crop rotation options, and make informed decisions that may improve soil health, conserve water, and strengthen agricultural resilience.

By connecting NASA's scientific data with real agricultural needs, FIELD SHIFT makes environmental information more accessible and supports a more sustainable future for farming.
details:
FIELD SHIFT – Detailed Project Description

FIELD SHIFT is a smart agricultural decision-support platform developed to help farmers make more informed and sustainable crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data and agricultural knowledge.

How Does It Work?

The platform allows farmers to select their farm location and explore environmental conditions that influence agricultural productivity. It uses NASA POWER climate data to examine factors such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation.

Our team also analyzed NASA MODIS datasets, including NDVI (MOD13Q1) and Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2), using NASA AppEEARS. These analyses help us better understand vegetation conditions and surface temperature patterns.

The platform prototype combines climate information with crop-related knowledge to support crop rotation recommendations. Farmers can explore potential crop choices and better understand environmental factors affecting their land.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FIELD SHIFT aims to:

  • Support informed crop rotation and crop selection.
  • Help farmers understand climate-related agricultural risks.
  • Encourage efficient water use and sustainable soil management.
  • Reduce uncertainty when planning future growing seasons.
  • Make NASA's scientific data more accessible to farmers.

Our long-term goal is to support agricultural resilience, particularly in regions experiencing water scarcity and increasing climate variability.

Tools and Technologies

We used several tools and technologies during development:

  • NASA POWER API: Climate data collection.
  • NASA MODIS: Vegetation indices and land surface temperature observations.
  • NASA AppEEARS: Satellite data extraction.
  • Python: Data processing, cleaning, and analysis.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Data manipulation and numerical calculations.
  • Matplotlib: Data visualization.
  • Google Colab: Data analysis and experimentation.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Website interface development.
  • FastAPI: Python-based backend development.

Creativity and Innovation

FIELD SHIFT connects space-based environmental information with practical agricultural decisions through an accessible platform.

Instead of presenting farmers with complex satellite datasets, our approach focuses on transforming scientific information into understandable climate insights and potential crop rotation recommendations.

The project also explores how different environmental indicators can contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of agricultural conditions.

Factors Considered

Our team considered several important factors:

  • Local temperature and seasonal climate patterns.
  • Rainfall variability and water scarcity.
  • Vegetation health and land surface temperature.
  • Crop suitability and rotation principles.
  • Soil health and long-term agricultural sustainability.
  • Data quality, availability, and limitations.
  • Accessibility and ease of use for farmers.

Current Limitations and Future Development

FIELD SHIFT is a prototype. While NASA POWER data supports the current climate analysis, additional MODIS analyses have not all been integrated into the platform.

Future development will focus on integrating SMAP soil moisture data, local soil properties, irrigation availability, and crop-specific requirements to improve the reliability and usefulness of recommendations.

Our vision is to turn NASA's Earth observation data into practical agricultural knowledge that helps farmers make smarter decisions and build a more sustainable future.

NASA MODIS – Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1 NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2 LST)
